Utility Locates Before Every Stump Grind

Stump grinding cuts several inches below grade, and Ohio law requires an underground utility locate through the Ohio Utilities Protection Service (OUPS, dial 8-1-1) before any digging or grinding. Roubic files that locate request ahead of every Shaker Heights job, so gas, water, electric, and communication lines are marked before the grinder starts. There is no separate filing burden on the homeowner.

For most existing stumps on private property in Shaker Heights, grinding does not trigger the city tree review that removing a standing, living tree can — you are removing what is already cut, not felling a specimen. Roubic confirms the specifics for your address during the free on-site walk.

What Happens If You Leave It

The Cost of Leaving a Stump — Shaker Heights Context

Three reasons a leftover Shaker Heights stump is worth grinding out sooner rather than later.

Regrowth & Suckering

Many species push new shoots and root suckers from a live stump for years. Left alone, a single stump can turn into a spreading thicket that is far harder to remove later.

Pest & Decay Harborage

A rotting stump attracts carpenter ants, beetles, and wood-decay fungi close to the house and other trees — a colony you would rather not host near a Shaker Heights foundation.

Trip & Mower Hazard

A low stump hidden in the lawn is a tripping hazard and a mower-blade killer. Grinding it below grade removes the obstacle and reclaims the usable yard.

Common Shaker Heights Stump Grinding Questions

Shaker Heights Stump Grinding FAQ

Six things Shaker Heights homeowners want to know before booking a grind.

Do I need a permit to grind a stump in Shaker Heights?
In most cases, no. Grinding an existing stump on private property removes wood that is already cut, so it generally does not trigger the city review that felling a standing, living tree can. What Ohio law does require is an underground utility locate — Roubic files the Ohio 811 (OUPS) request before every grind so buried gas, water, electric, and communication lines are marked first. Roubic confirms any address-specific requirements during the free on-site walk.
How much does stump grinding cost in Shaker Heights?
Every stump is different, so Roubic quotes grinding on-site in writing after Aaron sees it. Cost is driven by the stump's diameter and root flare, how far below grade you want it ground, how many stumps there are, whether the grindings are hauled off or backfilled, and how tight the access is. Estimates are always free.
How soon can Roubic grind a stump in Shaker Heights?
Shaker Heights is a Tier 2 Roubic service area, so free estimates are typically walked and grinding scheduled within about two business days of your request. Timing can shift with weather and workload, and storm or hazard emergencies are handled through the 24/7 line.
How deep do you grind the stump?
Standard grinding takes the stump down roughly four to six inches below grade, which is enough to reseed grass or lay sod over the spot. If you plan to replant a tree or install a bed in the same location, let Aaron know during the estimate and the crew can grind deeper and chase more of the surface roots.
What happens to the wood grindings and the hole?
Grinding produces a mound of wood chips and soil. By default Roubic rakes the grindings back into the hole to backfill it level, or hauls them off if you prefer — your choice, confirmed at the estimate. The area will settle over the following weeks as the buried grindings break down, so topping it off with soil before seeding is normal.
Is Roubic insured for stump grinding in Shaker Heights?
Yes — Roubic carries general liability insurance and workers-compensation coverage. A certificate of insurance is available on request and can be included in the estimate packet for jobs that require COI submission, such as property-manager or HOA work.
